title: Espacios Abiertos: The Territory Discount Program & The Cost of Uncertainty: The Federal Art of the Expiration Date
description: Medicaid comes in two versions. In the 50 states, Washington matches whatever qualifying care a state spends, between 50 and 83 cents on the dollar, with no ceiling. In Puerto Rico it comes with a fixed match and an annual cap, and once the cap runs out every additional dollar is 100% local. This episode reads El costo de la incertidumbre, the September 2026 paper by Espacios Abiertos, and follows the clock Congress set in the Consolidated Appropriations Act of 2023: a 76% federal match that expires on September 30, 2027 and falls to 55%; five statutory caps ending at $3.825 billion; and an FY2028 allotment ordered to be rebuilt from the FY2019 base, about $471 million, as if the last eight years of funding never happened. With coverage held constant, the island's own bill goes from about $1.4 billion to $4.85 billion, 35% of the General Fund. It is the same math GAO said the statute required in FY2022, written back in on purpose. Also: 1.35 million enrollees, the $500 million forward cost of benefits that only began in July 2024, the $164 million municipal bill that returns at 55%, the Governor's $4.415 billion ask at 83%, and why raising the match without lifting the cap only empties the cap faster.
